It is binary. And for the land beneath, the air above and the life around, it changes everything.|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20180217084317/https://www.economist.com/news/science-and-technology/21577341-worlds-third-largest-area-ice-about-undergo-systematic|archivedate=17 February 2018}}

#* {{quote-book|en|date=2010-03-15|author=Lance K. Erickson|title=Space Flight: History, Technology, and Operations|publisher=Government Institutes|isbn=9781605906843|page=145|text=Above the core is the lower-density liquid mantle composed of ice materials under high pressure and temperature. This massive liquid layer would not be separated into layers of traditional ice compounds, but mixtures of radically different compounds originally consisting of water, carbon dioxide, methane, and ammonia {{...}} Since the mass of the planet is dominated by the liquid mantle that itself consists of heated '''ices''' under pressure, both Uranus and Neptune are classified as giant '''ice''' planets.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|date=2010-12-02|author=Raymond T. Pierrehumbert|title=Principles of Planetary Climate|publisher=Cambridge University Press|isbn=9781139495066|page=20|text=Uranus and Neptune are {{...}} usually classified separately as ''ice giants'' because they contain a much higher proportion of ice-forming substances such as water, ammonia, and methane. {{...}} In the case of Uranus, the '''ice''' mantle must make up between 9.3 and 13.4 Earth masses worth of the total mass of the planet, which is 14.5 Earth masses. Similar proportions apply to Neptune. The commonly used term "'''ice''' mantle" is someone misleading, since the substance is actually a hot, slushy mixture that would be more aptly described as a water–ammonia ocean.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|title=Geophysical Exploration of the Solar System|passage=Neptune has one major moon: Triton, which is comparable in size to the Jovian moon Europa and at an average density of 2.061 g/cm{{sup|3}} widely understood to be covered by several hundred km of frozen or liquid '''ice'''.|year=2022|page=45|isbn=9780443186981|publisher=w:Elsevier|pageurl=https://www.google.ca/books/edition/Geophysical_Exploration_of_the_Solar_Sys/XZaDEAAAQBAJ?gbpv=1&pg=PA45}}
